correctness.rationale: The bilinear basis multiplication is exactly XY=r(X)c(Y)^T. The row-column margin map is a surjective linear map of rank m+n-1 with q^((m-1)(n-1)) equal lifts. Induction yields X^h=s^(h-2)rc^T; the exceptional zero-sum squares require a separate case. For nonzero total, rank-one identity (Z1)(1^TZ)=t(Z)Z forces compatible margins uniquely for each h-th root s of t(Z); there are gcd(h,q-1) such s. For zero total, squares have q-1 compatible outer product factorizations iff both margins vanish, whereas all powers h>=3 vanish. Zero-fiber counts follow by inclusion-exclusion or one linear equation. Counting rank-one outputs by normalized factors yields the claimed image formula. The independently written coefficient-wise full-multiplication checker passed all 29 input/target enumerations over q=2,3,4,5,9, including extension-field arithmetic; mass sums equal q^(mn). No finite experiment substitutes for the general algebraic proof.

value.rationale: An intrinsically motivated complete finite-field power-map invariant of the canonical rectangular-band semigroup algebra is established for every exponent, dimension and field order. The difference between squaring and every higher power has a geometric explanation: the rank-one cone inside the two zero-augmentation margin hyperplanes occurs among squares, is annihilated at the cube, and appears only for m,n>=2. Exact cardinalities and pointwise multiplicities are more informative than merely knowing the radical, the number of nilpotents or the field scalar root counts. This is not a selected numerical curiosity or mere notation change; it resolves a natural factorization question for the full family. The proof remains elementary, which is a positive feature and not itself a claim of major significance.
